title: DAEMON FORGE 003 — 180-second production stress proof
description: Independent technical composition, not DAEMON HEADLINER 001. 96 bars at 128 BPM, exactly 180 s, 15 tracks. Original arrangement using only existing V12 SIGNATURE and MORPH assets; licensing remains pending. Tests continuous absolute-frame playback, repitched sustained chords, glide, gates/chokes, gain/pan automation and unreset delay/reverb tails. Requires explicit --reuse-voices; legacy budget intentionally rejects it.

tracks.description: Tight SUB HAMMER groove; same-frame IRON PULSE layers coexist at arrivals.
Clap/snare backbeat, quiet displaced ghosts and authored build rolls.
Velocity-shaped sixteenths with delayed sixteenth positions and track-local open-hat chokes.
Low chrome motif and section identity; delay and reverb ring continuously across every section.
One mono low-end owner with authored absolute gain pumping and occasional continuous playback-rate slides.
High-passed mid-bass answers with repeated rate glides; no additional sub owner.
Broken four-note cell, its rhythm rotates by section; echoes continue over transitions.
Original two-bar question and answer; exposed middle and a changed second arrival.
Sustained open fifths run across bars, cache reuse and arbitrary timeline divisions without retrigger.
Voice-led three-note chords lasting two bars; repitched harmony drives the original interpolation budget above 1b.
Quiet long vowel phrases and contrary-motion answers; gain and pan move in absolute song time.
Last 3.75 seconds of the original riser align exactly to the four designed arrivals.
Sparse original impacts at structural arrivals; conservative gain over the mono sub.
MORPH cable-pluck pitched replies above the bass, high-passed to preserve low-end ownership.
Individually scheduled MORPH ratchet ticks; rhythmic acceleration, not a pre-rendered loop.
